title: Fix it: enrich orders with the customer that placed them
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

You are given `payload.orders`, an array of `{ orderId, customerId }`, and `payload.customers`, an array of `{ id, name }`.

Return an array of `{ orderId, customerId, customerName }`, one entry per order, in the order the orders appear.

If an order's `customerId` does not match any customer, `customerName` is `null`. A customer that no order references does not appear in the output at all.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
leftJoin(payload.orders, payload.customers, (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String)
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
returns leftJoin's raw {l, r} pairs instead of the merged shape the question asks for
solution:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
leftJoin(payload.orders, payload.customers, (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String)
  map { orderId: $.l.orderId, customerId: $.l.customerId, customerName: $.r.name }

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
leftJoin(payload.orders, payload.customers, (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String)

explanation.approach: `leftJoin` is not part of core DataWeave — it lives in `dw::core::Arrays` and has to be imported. Its job is narrower than 'give me the merged rows': it walks the left array and, for each item, attaches the right item whose key matches, if one exists. What comes back is a pair, `{l: ..., r: ...}` — one item from each side, never a single merged object — and when nothing on the right matches, the pair simply has no `r` at all rather than `r: null`. Turning that into the shape this question wants, and handling both edges — an order with no customer, and a customer no order points to — is the actual work.

snippets.label: Without the import, the name does not resolve
snippets.note: `leftJoin` is not in core. Calling it without `import * from dw::core::Arrays` is a compile error, not a runtime one.

snippets.label: What leftJoin actually returns: pairs, not merged rows
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
leftJoin(payload.orders, payload.customers, (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String)
snippets.note: Every element is `{l, r}` — the left order and the matched customer, sitting side by side rather than combined. Building `{ orderId, customerId, customerName }` out of this is a separate step.

snippets.label: An order with no matching customer has no r key at all
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
leftJoin([{orderId:'O3',customerId:99}], [{id:1,name:'Ann'}], (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String)
snippets.note: Customer 99 does not exist, so the pair for order O3 has an `l` and nothing else — there is no `r` field to be null, it is simply absent.

snippets.label: Selecting through the missing key still gives null
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
(leftJoin([{orderId:'O3',customerId:99}], [{id:1,name:'Ann'}], (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String))[0].r.name
snippets.note: `.r` is absent, and DataWeave selectors on a missing or null value keep returning null rather than erroring. `$.r.name` already does the right thing for an unmatched order with no extra handling.

snippets.label: The plausible wrong approach: a nested filter per row
snippets.note: This looks reasonable and passes on data where everything matches. But the trailing `filter` that was meant to clean up ends up deleting order O3 entirely, because it has no customer and so no way to tell 'unmatched' apart from 'exclude this row'. The question asked for O3 to appear with `customerName: null` — it just vanished instead.

snippets.label: The full answer
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
leftJoin(payload.orders, payload.customers, (o) -> o.customerId as String, (c) -> c.id as String)
  map { orderId: $.l.orderId, customerId: $.l.customerId, customerName: $.r.name }
snippets.note: The join finds the pairs; the `map` afterward flattens each `{l, r}` pair into the final shape, and `$.r.name` reads as null on its own for any order that had no match.
